nodes.name: In situ Ni(OH)₂ growth on MXene
nodes.procedure: Ni(NO₃)₂·6H₂O (0.9 mmol) was added to a three-necked round-bottom flask containing 20 mL of the Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene/NMP dispersion (2 mg mL⁻¹) followed by adding urea (2 mmol) and vigorously stirring for 30 min. The above suspension was then refluxed for 6 h at 100 °C under N₂ flow. Then, the Ni(OH)₂/Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene precursor was obtained by centrifugation, rinsed with deionized (DI) water and ethanol several times, and freeze-dried.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows characteristic peaks of NiO phase (JCPDS No. 47-1049) and Ni phase (JCPDS No. 04-0850), confirming coexistence of NiO and Ni in the heterostructure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After further annealing under a H₂/Ar atmosphere, the XRD patterns of the target product in Figure 3a show characteristic peaks that are clearly distinguishable as belonging to either the NiO phase (JCPDS No. 47-1049) or the Ni phase (JCPDS No. 04-0850).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p peaks at 854.0/871.8 eV (Ni⁰) and 855.9/873.6 eV (Ni²⁺) with negative shift vs Ni-NiO confirming electronic interactions; O 1s peaks at 529.43 eV (lattice O), 531.39 eV (O-vacancies), 533.32 eV (adsorbed O); Ti 2p and C 1s confirm MXene heterostructure formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the high-resolution Ni 2p spectrum (Figure 3b), the two peaks that are located at 854.0 and 871.8 eV are ascribed to Ni⁰ 2p₃/₂ and Ni⁰ 2p₁/₂ ... The high-resolution O 1s spectrum in Figure 3c can be divided into three peaks at 529.43, 531.39, and 533.32 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR shows strong peak at g=2.003 from unpaired electrons captured by oxygen vacancies, confirming higher Oᵥ concentration than Ni-NiO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As presented in Figure 3f, the Ni-NiO/Ti₃C₂TₓMXene exhibits a strong EPR peak at g = 2.003 originating from the unpaired electrons captured by Oᵥₛ.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectroscopy performed on samples; post-OER test shows new peaks at 475 and 561 cm⁻¹ attributed to Ni-O in NiOOH species confirming surface reconstruction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, Ni-NiO/Ti₃C₂TₓMXene Raman spectra were also obtained both before and after the OER stability test ... Both of the newly discovered peaks, located at 475 and 561 cm⁻¹ can be attributed to the Ni-O bond that is present in the NiOOH species.
